annotations.title: Compare pooled (M/M/c) vs separate (c × M/M/1) queueing

description: Run the classic operations-research teaching demo: pooled queueing (one shared queue, c servers) vs separate queues (c independent queues, one server each, λ/c traffic to each). Both runs have identical total capacity (c × μ) and identical total arrivals (λ), so the offered load ρ is the same; the only structural difference is whether arrivals share a queue or split into c isolated streams. The pooled configuration ALWAYS produces shorter waits — that's the whole teaching point. Use this when the user asks 'should we pool our resources?' / 'should we cross-train?' / 'why do banks have one line instead of c?' / 'what's the cost of siloing my call center into specialist queues?'. Returns both runs side by side with the pooled-vs-separate wait delta. ANTI-FABRICATION: numbers come from two real DES runs. Quote them VERBATIM.

arrivalRate.description: Mean total arrival rate (λ). Pooled run takes all of it; separate run divides evenly across the c queues.

servers.description: Number of servers (c). Pooled: one queue feeds all c. Separate: c independent queues, each with one server and λ/c traffic. Range 2-50 (with c=1 there's nothing to compare).

serviceRate.description: Mean service rate per server (μ, customers/hour each server finishes). Identical across both runs.

simulationDays.description: Days to simulate (same for both runs). Range 1-30.

name: compare_separate_vs_pooled
